__comment: Combined per manager request: applications-monitor.json, nx-applications-dashboard.json, and nx-applications-monitoring.json all queried the same metric family (container_cpu/memory/network_*, kube_pod_container_status_ready/restarts) at three different granularities (fleet health / namespace-wide aggregate / per-service detail) - combined into one dashboard with those three as collapsible sections instead of three separate files, all sharing one $datasource + $namespace picker. BUGS FIXED while merging: (1) applications-monitor.json's Fleet Health panels queried an exact hardcoded snapshot of pod names including their ReplicaSet hash suffix (e.g. 'applications-archiver-789855dc6d-ngx9v') - those hashes change on every deploy, so this was already stale and would show 'Bad'/'No data' for current pods. Rebuilt as a dynamic label_values() query against $namespace, no hardcoded pod list. (2) nx-applications-dashboard.json's panels used gridPos w:30, exceeding Grafana's 24-column grid (always rendered clipped/overflowing), and its last two panels (Pod Count / Pod Restarts) overlapped by 2 grid units - re-tiled as a clean 2-column layout. (3) nx-applications-monitoring.json's 60 panels (15 services x 4 panels) had no row headers at all, just implicit grouping by title prefix - added one collapsible row divider per service for real navigability. | Folded in the 4 genuinely new panels from Application Health Executive View (Request Rate, Request Latency p95, HTTP Success Rate, Services Down by name) as a new top row - its other panels (Services Up count, Overall Fleet Health %, CPU Usage by Pod, Hourly Request Volume) duplicated what Fleet Health Summary / All-Pods Resource Overview already cover here, so those were not re-added. application-health-executive.json deleted as a duplicate. | 2026-09-18: folded in Applications V2 - Overview (the per-connector/per-service Pods Up drill-down index, 80 panels) as an additional section, so there is one Applications Overview dashboard instead of two. Its drill-down links already point at Connectors Detail / Services Detail. Recomputed gridPos block-by-block while merging - the source file had a pre-existing row/tile overlap bug (Credential Manager row overlapped the prior Box-Content block).

panels.title: 🚦 Request Golden Signals & Down Services (folded in from Application Health Executive View)
Request Latency p95 by Service (where instrumented)
panels.description: http_request_duration_seconds is opt-in per service (pipeline-lib-go's shared HTTP metric set) - not every service installs it. Blank for a service means it hasn't wired up the shared HTTP metrics, not that it's slow.

panels.title: Services Down (instant)
panels.description: Any service currently reporting up == 0, named by job. The Fleet Health Summary row below gives you counts; this names which one.

panels.title: $pods
panels.description: Pod Ready status: 1 = Good, 0 = Bad

panels.title: Pods Good vs Bad (count)
panels.description: Percentage of pods in the selected namespace that are Good (Ready) vs Bad (Not Ready)

targets.expr: count(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"})) - sum(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"}))

panels.title: Pods OK and Bad (count)
panels.description: Counts of pods in the selected namespace that are Ready (OK) vs Not Ready (Bad)

targets.expr: count(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"})) - sum(min by (pod) (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="$namespace", pod!~"grafana-dashboard.*"}))

panels.title: 🔗 V2 Migrated Components — Pods Up (drill-down index into Connectors/Services Detail)
Error Rate
panels.description: Non-OK gRPC responses per second. Filtered on the numeric code label rather than status, which is free text including the error message.

panels.title: Round-Trip p95
panels.description: Job creation through result consumed from NATS, on the service's own 0.1s-300s ladder — a different scale from the HTTP/gRPC latency histograms because a connection test is dispatched asynchronously and can run for minutes. Only counts round trips that completed: a result that never arrives shows up as a drop in observation count, not a latency spike.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Connection-test creations that failed, per second. This is a dispatch-side failure; a test that dispatches fine but never comes back shows up as stalled on the request-service overview, not here.

panels.title: Ingested (rate)
panels.description: outcome="forwarded" only — the one outcome that means a document was actually ingested.

panels.title: Not Ingested
panels.description: outcome="failed_permanent" — documents knowledge-service gave up on. NOT a drop rate: the item is still forwarded downstream carrying its failure in knowledge_hub. Retryable conditions never appear here — they are retried in-process until they resolve, so this counter only moves on a terminal verdict.

panels.title: Scan p95
panels.description: ScanStart discovery + fan-out phase, on a 0.5s–1024s ladder. Not whole-scan duration.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Query failures against the source database only. Skipped tables, inline fallbacks and connector panics are counted apart — see the MySQL overview's Silent-Failure Signals row.

panels.title: Ingested (rate)
panels.description: outcome="succeeded" only — the one outcome that wrote a document. "reused" is a same-checksum short-circuit and is deliberately excluded.

panels.title: Failed (rate)
panels.description: Classified failures. Split by phase on the Ingestion dashboard — a pre-mutation failure costs nothing, a mid-write one leaves a document that used to be retrievable and is not now.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Connect codes other than "ok". This is the wire outcome, not the ingestion verdict.

panels.title: Fan-out p95
panels.description: ScanStart discovery + fan-out phase, on a 50ms–~102s ladder. Not whole-scan duration.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Failures against the source database only: schema-listing failures on a DatabaseFork plus per-table scan and publish failures.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(postgresql_connector_database_errors_total{namespace="$namespace"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(postgresql_connector_table_errors_total{namespace="$namespace"}[5m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(postgresql_connector_columns_failed_total{namespace="$namespace"}[5m])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Fetch p95
panels.description: Successful fetches only (success="true").

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Every error_code summed. The NAK_* codes were redelivered with no reply sent; the FETCH_ERROR_* codes were answered with an error response.

panels.title: Pods Up
panels.description: Every connector resolves its credentials through this pod over gRPC.

panels.title: JWKS Available
panels.description: 0 means the UI-facing Connect API is rejecting every request. It does not mean this service is down: the gRPC CredentialService connectors depend on never touches the JWKS, which is why this is a metric rather than a health check. The p95 and error rate beside it are that gRPC surface, so a JWKS outage should leave them flat.

panels.title: Credential Lookup p95
panels.description: gRPC, the surface connectors call. Every connector blocks on this before it can read anything.

panels.title: Error Rate
panels.description: Non-OK gRPC codes, matching how Registration Service reports its error rate.
